haas_alarms.title: MACHINE NOT HOMED
haas_alarms.description: The machine axes have not been homed since power-up. All programs requiring absolute position are blocked.
possible_causes: Homing was interrupted by alarm or E-Stop
solutions: Press POWER/RESTART then press ZERO RET to home all axes
Ensure no alarms are active before homing
Check that E-Stop is released before starting homing sequence

haas_alarms.title: LOW AIR PRESSURE
haas_alarms.description: Shop air supply pressure is below the minimum required for machine operation (pneumatic systems, ATC, coolant).
solutions: Verify air compressor is running and has adequate capacity
Check main air supply valve is fully open
Inspect air lines for leaks or kinks
Replace or clean air filter/regulator
Minimum required pressure: 90 PSI / 6.2 bar

haas_alarms.title: SERVO ERROR TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The axis position following error exceeded the maximum allowed value. The motor cannot keep up with the commanded position.
possible_causes: Mechanical binding or obstruction on the axis
Worn or damaged ballscrew, linear guides, or bearings
Excessive feed rate or acceleration settings
solutions: Power off and check for mechanical binding — move axis by hand
Inspect ballscrew, linear guides, wipers, and bearings
Reduce rapid override to 25% and test — if alarm clears, check parameters
Check servo drive LEDs for secondary fault codes
Check Parameters 15 and 16 (following error limits)
Verify correct lubrication on all axes

haas_alarms.title: SERVO DRIVE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The servo amplifier/drive has detected an internal fault condition.
possible_causes: Short circuit in motor or cables
solutions: Power cycle the machine and monitor if alarm returns
Check servo drive LEDs for specific fault code
Inspect motor cables for damage or shorts
Verify cabinet cooling fans are operational
Check incoming power voltage and stability

haas_alarms.title: AXIS NOT HOMED
haas_alarms.description: A program or function was requested that requires the machine to be homed first.
possible_causes: Machine was powered on but axes were not homed
E-Stop or alarm occurred during homing
solutions: Press POWER/RESTART, then press ZERO RET to home all axes
If home switch fault, check Parameters 22 and 1 for home direction/offset
Verify home switch signals in Diagnostics > Inputs

haas_alarms.title: AXIS MOTOR OVERLOAD
haas_alarms.description: The axis motor current draw exceeded the overload limit. Thermal or current overload protection activated.
possible_causes: Worn ballscrew or bearings requiring more force
Crash or tool contact with fixture
solutions: Power off and check for mechanical obstruction on the affected axis
Lubricate ballscrews and linear guides
Allow machine to cool for 30 minutes before restarting
Check for loose motor coupling
Inspect and replace worn ballscrew/bearings if needed

haas_alarms.title: DRIVE OVER TEMPERATURE
haas_alarms.description: A servo amplifier reached its thermal limit. The drive will shut down to prevent damage.
possible_causes: Drive has been overloaded for extended period
solutions: Allow machine to cool — wait 30-60 minutes before restart
Check all cabinet cooling fans are spinning correctly
Clean dust from drive heat sinks and cabinet vents
Verify ambient temperature is within specification (< 40 C)
Reduce duty cycle or cutting loads

haas_alarms.title: SERVO DRIVE DISCONNECT
haas_alarms.description: Communication between the CNC and servo drive was lost.
possible_causes: Loose or damaged servo drive communication cable
Power supply issue to the drive
solutions: Check servo drive cable connections at both the drive and the MOCON/IOPCB
Power cycle the machine fully (main breaker off, wait 30s, on)
Inspect cables for pinching or damage

haas_alarms.title: HARD LIMIT — POSITIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: An axis reached its positive hard travel limit switch.
possible_causes: Program error causing axis to exceed travel boundary
solutions: Jog axis away from limit switch in negative direction
Check work offset coordinates — tool may be positioned outside workpiece area
Verify G-code coordinates are within machine travel limits
Check limit switch input signal in Diagnostics

haas_alarms.title: HARD LIMIT — NEGATIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: An axis reached its negative hard travel limit switch.
possible_causes: Program error causing axis to travel past negative boundary
solutions: Jog axis away from limit switch in positive direction
Verify work offsets and tool length offsets are set correctly
Check G-code for incorrect negative coordinate values

haas_alarms.title: TOOL OFFSET NOT SET
haas_alarms.description: A G43 tool length compensation call references an H offset that is zero or not set.
possible_causes: Tool not measured or manually entered
Wrong H number in G43 command
solutions: Measure the tool with the tool setter and enter length in offset table
Verify the H number matches the tool offset entry number
Use G43 H[tool_number] matching your tool setup

haas_alarms.title: OVER TRAVEL — POSITIVE Z
haas_alarms.description: The Z axis exceeded its positive software or hardware travel limit.
possible_causes: Program commanded Z too high above home
Tool length offset incorrect or not loaded
solutions: Jog Z axis down (negative direction) to clear limit
Verify tool length offsets are measured and active (G43 H_)
Check Z work offset value in G54-G59 offsets table
Review program for incorrect positive Z values

haas_alarms.title: OVER TRAVEL — NEGATIVE Z
haas_alarms.description: The Z axis exceeded its negative software or hardware travel limit.
possible_causes: Program depth exceeds machine Z travel
Tool length offset not active — all Z moves go too deep
Work offset Z incorrectly set near machine limit
solutions: Jog Z axis up (positive direction) to clear limit
Ensure G43 H_ is active before all Z cutting moves
Verify Z work offset is correctly measured from part surface
Check all Z depth values in program

haas_alarms.title: OVER TRAVEL — X AXIS
haas_alarms.description: The X axis exceeded its software or hardware travel limit.
possible_causes: Program X coordinates outside machine travel range
Work offset X value places origin outside usable area
G-code with incremental moves accumulating past limit
solutions: Jog X axis back within travel limits
Recheck work offset X position
Verify all X coordinates in program are within machine travel
Check for incremental (G91) moves that exceed travel

haas_alarms.title: SOFT LIMIT — POSITIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: The programmed move would exceed the positive software travel limit.
possible_causes: Incorrect work offset placed near edge of travel
Tool length offset not applied, causing Z overtravel
solutions: Verify work offset (G54) is correctly set — it may be too close to machine limits
Check all axis coordinates in the program relative to machine travel
Ensure tool length offset is loaded (G43 H_) before Z moves
Review soft limit Parameters (43-48)

haas_alarms.title: SOFT LIMIT — NEGATIVE DIRECTION
haas_alarms.description: The programmed move would exceed the negative software travel limit.
possible_causes: Program has excessive negative Z depth
solutions: Check Z work offset — if set at zero instead of actual surface, all Z moves will be too deep
Verify tool length offset is active (G43 H_)
Reduce depth-of-cut values in program

haas_alarms.title: E-STOP — EMERGENCY STOP
haas_alarms.description: Emergency stop was activated. All motion has been halted.
possible_causes: Safety door was opened during a cycle
Servo fault triggered the E-STOP chain
solutions: Investigate and resolve the cause of the E-STOP before resetting
Twist the E-STOP button clockwise to release it
Press RESET to clear the alarm
Check for other active alarms that may have caused the E-STOP
Check safety door interlock switch if door-related

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE MOTOR OVERHEAT
haas_alarms.description: The spindle motor temperature sensor has detected overheating. Spindle operation is blocked until the motor cools.
possible_causes: Continuous heavy cutting without adequate cool-down time
High ambient temperature in machine enclosure
solutions: Stop machining and allow spindle to idle or stop for 15-30 minutes
Check spindle motor cooling fan is functioning
Reduce spindle speed and cutting load
Inspect spindle bearings for noise or excessive play
Verify spindle motor temperature sensor is functional

haas_alarms.title: TOOL NUMBER TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The T number in the program exceeds the number of pockets in the tool changer.
possible_causes: Program written for a machine with more pockets
Incorrect T number typed in program
Machine parameter for tool count is set incorrectly
solutions: Check T number in program — it must not exceed the number of available pockets
Verify machine tool capacity in Parameter 65
Update program with valid tool numbers

haas_alarms.title: NO TOOL IN SPINDLE
haas_alarms.description: An M06 tool change was commanded but the spindle does not contain the expected tool.
possible_causes: Tool was manually removed from spindle
Previous tool change did not complete correctly
ATC carousel is out of sync
solutions: Manually insert the correct tool into the spindle
Use ATC recovery to synchronize the carousel
Check ATC pocket sensors and verify tool presence detection

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE NOT ORIENTED
haas_alarms.description: The spindle did not reach its orientation position before tool change.
possible_causes: Heavy tool causing spindle to coast too far
solutions: Check spindle encoder signal in Diagnostics
Verify orient speed Parameter (Parameters 257, 258)
Check spindle brake operation
Power cycle and retry — orient failure can be intermittent

haas_alarms.title: MISSING FEEDRATE
haas_alarms.description: A cutting motion (G01, G02, G03) was commanded without an active feedrate (F word).
possible_causes: F word missing from the program block
Modal feedrate was cleared without being reset
solutions: Add an F word to the first cutting move: G01 X_ Y_ F100.
Verify F value is non-zero
Check that G94 (feed per minute) or G95 (feed per rev) is active as expected

haas_alarms.title: DIVIDE BY ZERO
haas_alarms.description: A program calculation resulted in division by zero.
possible_causes: Macro variable used as divisor is zero or uninitialized
Formula in G-code macro has zero denominator
solutions: Review custom macro code for division operations
Add a check: IF [#VAR NE 0] before dividing
Initialize all macro variables to safe values at program start

haas_alarms.title: SUBPROGRAM NOT FOUND
haas_alarms.description: An M98 call references a subprogram that cannot be found in memory or on the device.
possible_causes: Subprogram was not loaded to the machine
Incorrect P number in M98 call
solutions: Load the subprogram to the machine memory
Verify P number in M98 matches the actual program number O_ of the subprogram
Check if subprogram is on USB or NetShare — machine may not be searching there

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE LOAD MONITOR
haas_alarms.description: Spindle load exceeded the programmed threshold. Cycle may have been halted.
possible_causes: Feed rate too high for material and tool
solutions: Inspect and replace the cutting tool
Reduce feed rate and/or depth of cut
Check Material Override and Tool Load Monitor settings
Verify spindle load limit Parameter (setting 84)

haas_alarms.title: DOOR OPEN DURING CYCLE
haas_alarms.description: The machine door interlock detected the door is open while a cycle is running.
possible_causes: Safety door opened by operator during cycle
Door latch or interlock switch malfunction
solutions: Close the safety door completely and press CYCLE START
Check door latch mechanism for proper engagement
Test door switch signal in Diagnostics > Inputs
Do NOT bypass the interlock — safety hazard

haas_alarms.title: PARAMETER OUT OF RANGE
haas_alarms.description: A parameter value entered is outside the allowed range for that parameter.
possible_causes: Manual parameter entry with invalid value
solutions: Identify which parameter triggered the alarm (noted on screen)
Check Haas documentation for valid range of that parameter
Enter a valid value within the specified range

haas_alarms.title: HOME SWITCH NOT FOUND
haas_alarms.description: The home switch was not detected during the homing (zero return) sequence.
possible_causes: Axis moved past the switch location
solutions: Check home switch wiring connections at both the switch and the I/O board
Test home switch signal in Diagnostics > Inputs
Verify Parameter 1 (zero return direction) is set correctly
Manually trigger the switch with a screwdriver to test

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE FEEDBACK FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The spindle tachometer or encoder feedback signal is missing or out of range.
possible_causes: Spindle encoder cable disconnected or damaged
solutions: Check spindle encoder cable at the encoder and drive connection
Inspect cable for damage or pinching
Verify encoder supply voltage
Power cycle and monitor — intermittent encoder issues may recur
Replace encoder if signal is consistently missing

haas_alarms.title: ATC ARM FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic tool changer arm encountered a fault during tool change.
possible_causes: Heavy or oversized tool jammed the ATC
Tool not fully seated in pocket
solutions: Do NOT force the ATC manually — follow the ATC recovery procedure
Press ZERO RET to run ATC recovery sequence
Check air pressure supply (minimum 90 PSI / 6.2 bar)
Inspect ATC arm sensor signals in Diagnostics
Ensure all tools are properly seated and within weight limits

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE ENCODER FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The spindle position encoder has a hardware fault or lost signal.
possible_causes: Encoder cable broken or connector loose
solutions: Inspect spindle encoder connector — check for coolant damage
Check encoder cable routing for pinching or chafing
Clean or replace encoder if contaminated
Verify shielding on encoder cable is properly grounded

haas_alarms.title: LOW LUBE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic lubrication system is low on lubricant or has a fault.
solutions: Check the lube reservoir level and refill with recommended way oil (ISO VG 32)
Prime the lube pump manually using the purge button
Inspect lube lines for kinks or blockages
Check the lube pump output pressure
Do not run machine long without lubrication — causes guide and screw damage

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE DRIVE FAULT — DETAILED
haas_alarms.description: A specific fault code was detected in the spindle drive. Check the spindle drive display for the secondary code.
solutions: Read and record the spindle drive fault code from the drive display
Power cycle the machine (main breaker off, wait 60s, on)
Verify three-phase input power quality
Check spindle motor insulation resistance
Consult Haas spindle drive fault code table

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE DRIVE OVERLOAD
haas_alarms.description: The spindle drive detected sustained overcurrent — the spindle was overloaded beyond its rated capacity.
possible_causes: Cutting too aggressively in hard material
Drive current limit set too low
solutions: Reduce spindle load — lower depth of cut, feed rate, or speed
Inspect and replace cutting tool
Check spindle drive current limit parameters
Allow drive to cool before restarting

haas_alarms.title: ATC: CAROUSEL NOT AT HOME
haas_alarms.description: The ATC carousel failed to return to its home position after a tool change operation.
possible_causes: Air supply insufficient for carousel actuator
solutions: Check air pressure (minimum 90 PSI)
Inspect carousel for mechanical obstruction
Verify carousel home sensor signal in Diagnostics
Follow ATC recovery procedure to re-home carousel
Check carousel motor and drive

haas_alarms.title: LOW MEMORY
haas_alarms.description: The program memory is nearly full. New programs cannot be loaded.
possible_causes: Many large programs stored in memory
solutions: Back up programs to USB or network share
Delete programs that are no longer needed
Use the DNC (direct numerical control) mode for large programs instead of loading to memory

haas_alarms.title: LOW BATTERY
haas_alarms.description: The backup battery for memory retention is low and needs replacement.
possible_causes: Battery at end of life (typically 3-5 years)
solutions: Replace the 3.6V lithium backup battery as soon as possible
Do NOT power off the machine until battery is replaced — memory could be lost
After replacement, verify parameters and offsets are still intact
Part number: Haas 32-0261 (or equivalent 3.6V 1/2AA lithium)

haas_alarms.title: X AXIS SERVO ERROR TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The X axis position following error exceeded the maximum permitted value during motion or at rest.
possible_causes: X axis mechanical binding or obstruction
Worn X axis ballscrew or linear guides
solutions: Power off and check X axis for mechanical binding — move by hand
Lubricate X axis ballscrew and linear guides
Inspect X axis servo drive for fault indicators
Reduce rapid override and test
Check X axis servo tuning parameters

haas_alarms.title: Y AXIS SERVO ERROR TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The Y axis position following error exceeded the maximum permitted value.
possible_causes: Worn Y axis ballscrew or guides
solutions: Power off and check Y axis movement by hand for binding
Lubricate Y axis components
Check Y axis servo drive fault LEDs
Reduce feed rates and test

haas_alarms.title: AXIS DRIVER OVERTEMPERATURE
haas_alarms.description: A servo amplifier (axis driver) is overheating. The drive will derate or shut down.
possible_causes: Cabinet cooling fans failed or blocked
Excessive cutting load for extended period
Drive heat sink fins clogged with dust
solutions: Allow machine to cool 30-60 minutes before restarting
Clean all cabinet cooling fans and heat sink fins
Verify all fans are running in the electrical cabinet
Check room ambient temperature — max 40 C (104 F)
Reduce aggressive cutting cycles

haas_alarms.title: A AXIS SERVO ERROR TOO LARGE
haas_alarms.description: The A (rotary) axis position following error exceeded the maximum permitted value.
possible_causes: A axis mechanical binding or brake not releasing
solutions: Check A axis brake release signal
Inspect rotary table for mechanical obstruction
Verify A axis servo drive status
Check A axis following error parameter settings

haas_alarms.title: ENCODER HARDWARE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: An axis position encoder has a hardware fault — the signal is missing, corrupted, or indicates a hardware error.
possible_causes: Encoder damaged by coolant or chips
solutions: Inspect encoder connector for coolant contamination
Check encoder cable for damage near motor
Clean encoder connector pins with electrical contact cleaner
Replace encoder if signal cannot be restored

haas_alarms.title: LINEAR SCALE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: An optional linear scale (glass or magnetic) feedback device has a fault or lost signal.
possible_causes: Scale read head misaligned or damaged
Scale contaminated with coolant or chips
solutions: Clean linear scale and read head with dry air
Check read head alignment — should be within specification
Inspect scale cable for damage
Test signal with oscilloscope if available
Replace read head if signal is absent

haas_alarms.title: OVER TEMPERATURE WARNING
haas_alarms.description: An internal temperature sensor in the machine electrical cabinet detected elevated temperature.
possible_causes: Cabinet door left open (reduces cooling airflow)
solutions: Close all cabinet doors
Check all cooling fans are operating
Clean dust from all filters and vents
Verify ambient temperature is within spec
Allow machine to cool before continuing heavy work

haas_alarms.title: COOLANT LEVEL LOW
haas_alarms.description: The coolant tank level is below the minimum sensor threshold.
possible_causes: Coolant evaporated or was consumed during cutting
solutions: Refill coolant tank with properly mixed coolant (check concentration)
Inspect for coolant leaks around pump, hoses, and fittings
Check coolant concentration with refractometer — aim for 8-10% for most materials
Inspect coolant drain plug

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE DRIVE FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The spindle drive (VFD/inverter) has detected an internal fault condition.
possible_causes: Spindle motor overload or short circuit
Input power fault (voltage drop or phase loss)
solutions: Power cycle the machine completely (main breaker off, wait 30s)
Check spindle drive display for fault code — document and look up in Haas service manual
Verify three-phase power supply is balanced and within spec
Check spindle motor winding resistance
Ensure spindle brake is released before running

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE OVERLOAD
haas_alarms.description: The spindle motor load exceeded the overload threshold.
possible_causes: Feed rate or depth of cut too aggressive
solutions: Inspect and replace cutting tool
Reduce feed rate using feed override
Reduce depth of cut or step-over
Improve chip evacuation with coolant and air blast
Check spindle load limit setting (Setting 84)

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE SPEED ERROR
haas_alarms.description: The spindle could not reach or maintain the commanded speed within the allowed time.
possible_causes: Spindle load too high — stalled or near stall
Encoder fault — spindle speed feedback incorrect
solutions: Reduce programmed spindle speed and load
Check spindle encoder signal and wiring
Inspect belt condition and tension (if belt-drive model)
Check spindle drive for fault codes

haas_alarms.title: CHIP CONVEYOR FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The chip conveyor has detected a fault — it may be jammed, overloaded, or have a motor fault.
possible_causes: Large chip accumulation jamming the conveyor
Conveyor belt tension too tight or too loose
Chip type not suitable for conveyor design
solutions: Clear chip accumulation from the conveyor manually (machine off)
Check and adjust belt tension
Reset conveyor motor overload (thermal reset button near motor)
Break up large chips before they enter the conveyor

haas_alarms.title: AIR PRESSURE LOW
haas_alarms.description: Machine air supply pressure dropped below minimum threshold during operation.
possible_causes: Air compressor can't keep up with demand
solutions: Check air supply pressure at machine regulator (should be 90-100 PSI)
Drain and clean the air filter/regulator
Inspect pneumatic lines for leaks (use soap solution)
Ensure compressor is large enough for machine requirements

haas_alarms.title: SPINDLE ORIENT FAILURE
haas_alarms.description: The spindle failed to reach the orient position for tool change within the timeout period.
possible_causes: Orient speed or timeout parameter set incorrectly
Spindle encoder or position sensor fault
Heavy tool assembly with high inertia
solutions: Check Parameters 257 and 258 (orient speed and direction)
Increase orient timeout Parameter if using heavy tooling
Verify spindle encoder signal
Test spindle brake engagement

haas_alarms.title: SERVO DRIVE FAULT — GENERAL
haas_alarms.description: A servo drive has reported a general fault. Check the drive fault LED indicators for a specific code.
solutions: Read and record the LED blink code from the servo drive
Power cycle the machine completely
Check incoming DC bus voltage to drives
Inspect motor and cable connections
Contact Haas service if drive fault recurs

haas_alarms.title: E-STOP CIRCUIT OPEN
haas_alarms.description: The E-Stop safety chain has an open circuit — the safety relay is not energized.
possible_causes: Light curtain or safety mat triggered
solutions: Check and release any pressed E-Stop buttons (twist clockwise)
Close all safety doors
Verify light curtains and safety mats are unobstructed
Trace E-Stop chain with electrical drawings to find open contact

haas_alarms.title: DOOR INTERLOCK FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The safety door position switch has failed or shows inconsistent state.
solutions: Check door latch engages fully — door must close completely
Inspect door switch alignment and mounting
Test door switch continuity with multimeter
Check door switch wiring harness for damage

haas_alarms.title: LUBE PRESSURE LOW
haas_alarms.description: The way lube system oil pressure is below the minimum required threshold.
possible_causes: Way lube oil reservoir low or empty
solutions: Check and refill way lube oil reservoir
Test lube pump operation manually
Inspect lube lines for cracks or disconnected fittings
Check lube pressure switch operation

haas_alarms.title: COOLANT PUMP FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The coolant pump motor has detected a fault — overload, short, or loss of signal.
possible_causes: Low coolant level causing pump cavitation
solutions: Clean coolant pump intake strainer
Check coolant level
Reset pump motor overload (thermal protector reset)
Check pump motor wiring
Replace pump if motor has failed

haas_alarms.title: TOOL BREAK DETECTED
haas_alarms.description: The spindle load monitoring system or tool break sensor detected a tool failure.
possible_causes: Tool broken or chipped during cutting
Feed rate or depth of cut too aggressive for tool
solutions: Stop cycle and inspect tool in spindle
Replace broken or worn tool
Verify cutting parameters are appropriate for tool and material
Check tool break detection sensitivity settings

haas_alarms.title: ATC FAULT
haas_alarms.description: The automatic tool changer has encountered a general fault condition.
possible_causes: Tool changer arm or carousel is jammed
Tool not latched in carousel pocket
solutions: Follow the Haas ATC Recovery Procedure (see programming manual)
Check air pressure supply (must be >= 90 PSI / 6.2 bar)
Inspect ATC carousel for jammed tools or debris
Check all ATC sensor inputs in Diagnostics
Do not manually force the ATC mechanism

haas_alarms.title: ENCODER BATTERY LOW
haas_alarms.description: The absolute encoder battery backup voltage is low. Position data may be lost on next power cycle.
possible_causes: Encoder battery at end of life
solutions: Replace encoder battery before powering off machine
Note: if machine is powered off with dead encoder battery, all axes must be re-homed
Battery type: typically 3.6V lithium
After replacement, verify axis positions are correct

haas_alarms.title: TOOL POSITION ERROR
haas_alarms.description: The ATC carousel is not in the expected position or a tool was not found in the expected pocket.
possible_causes: ATC carousel lost position (power interruption during tool change)
solutions: Run ATC recovery: press ZERO RET or use the ATC FWD/REV keys carefully
Verify all tools are in their programmed T positions
Use ATC > CAROUSEL to manually position and verify pocket locations
Check carousel home sensor signal

haas_alarms.title: MACRO VARIABLE OUT OF RANGE
haas_alarms.description: A macro variable value is outside the valid range for the operation being performed.
possible_causes: Macro calculation produced a value beyond 32-bit integer or floating point range
solutions: Review custom macro program for variable range issues
Add bounds checking to macro calculations
Initialize all used macro variables at the start of the macro
Verify variable number is correct (#1-#10000 range)

haas_alarms.title: DIVISION BY ZERO IN MACRO
haas_alarms.description: A macro program executed a division where the divisor was zero.
possible_causes: Macro variable used as denominator has value zero
Uninitialized macro variable (default value 0) used in division
solutions: Add conditional check before division: IF [#VAR NE 0]
Initialize denominator variables to safe non-zero values
Review macro logic to prevent zero-value divisors

haas_alarms.title: G-CODE NOT RECOGNIZED
haas_alarms.description: The program contains a G-code that is not recognized or not supported on this machine.
possible_causes: Program written for a different machine or controller
Optional G-code feature not installed on this machine
solutions: Verify G-code number is correct
Check Haas G-code reference for supported codes on your machine model
Check if required option (e.g., high-speed machining, 5-axis) is installed

haas_alarms.title: TOOL LIFE EXCEEDED
haas_alarms.description: Tool Life Management indicates the tool has reached its programmed usage limit.
possible_causes: Tool has been used for the full programmed life (time or cycles)
Tool Life Management feature is active and has flagged the tool
solutions: Replace the tool in the ATC pocket with a fresh tool
Reset tool life counter for that tool number
Review and adjust tool life limits if they are too conservative or too aggressive

sinumerik_alarms.title: Emergency stop activated
sinumerik_alarms.description: The Emergency Stop button has been pressed or the E-STOP chain has been interrupted.
solutions: Identify and resolve the cause of the E-STOP before clearing
Release the E-STOP button (twist clockwise)
Press RESET on the operator panel
Check the PLC diagnostics for the E-STOP chain signal
Check all safety door and light curtain statuses

sinumerik_alarms.title: Following error too large
sinumerik_alarms.description: The position following error (difference between command and actual position) of an axis exceeded the maximum tolerance.
possible_causes: Mechanical binding, friction, or axis obstruction
Drive enable signal missing or drive fault
solutions: Check for mechanical obstruction — move axis by hand (machine off)
Verify the drive enable signal is active in PLC I/O
Check the KV (servo gain) parameters using Siemens startup tools
Inspect lubrication of guides and ballscrews
Check for additional drive alarms (380xxx series)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis cannot be moved
sinumerik_alarms.description: The axis is in a state where movement is not permitted. Drive enable is missing or axis has a blocking condition.
possible_causes: Drive enable signal from PLC not set
solutions: Check DB21 drive enable bits in PLC diagnostics
Verify safety relay and E-Stop chain are satisfied
Clear active alarms and check axis enable logic
Check PLC ladder for conditions inhibiting axis movement

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis at software travel limit
sinumerik_alarms.description: The axis position has reached or would exceed the programmed software travel limit.
possible_causes: Program position outside defined work area
Incorrect work offset placing tool outside limits
solutions: Jog axis back within the software limits
Verify work zero offset is correct
Check software limit machine data (MD36100, MD36110)
Verify axis homing position is correct

sinumerik_alarms.title: Contour monitoring: velocity too high
sinumerik_alarms.description: The actual axis velocity exceeded the contour monitoring tolerance band.
solutions: Emergency stop the machine
Check encoder wiring and polarity
Verify drive enable chain is correct
Check for additional drive alarms

sinumerik_alarms.title: Controller enable missing
sinumerik_alarms.description: The hardware enable signal for axis control is not present. Axis movement is not possible.
possible_causes: PLC has not released the axis enable (DB21 bit not set)
solutions: Check and reset the Emergency Stop
Close all safety doors and reset interlocks
Check PLC ladder for axis enable logic (DB21)
Verify safety relay output signal

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool data error
sinumerik_alarms.description: The active tool or offset data (T/D values) contains invalid or inconsistent data.
possible_causes: Tool geometry not entered in tool management
solutions: Check and enter correct tool geometry in tool management
Verify the D-number (cutting edge) corresponds to existing data
Check tool type matches the operation (drilling, milling, etc.)
Re-enter tool data completely

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool life expired
sinumerik_alarms.description: The tool life monitoring system has determined the active tool has reached its end of life.
possible_causes: Tool has reached its programmed life limit (time, parts, or wear)
Tool was not replaced after life expired
Life counter not reset after tool change
solutions: Replace the physical tool with a new one
Reset the tool life counter in tool management
Define a sister/replacement tool for automatic substitution
Adjust life limit values based on actual tool performance

sinumerik_alarms.title: NC program syntax error
sinumerik_alarms.description: A syntax error was detected in the NC part program. The control cannot decode the block.
possible_causes: Missing or incorrect address letter (G, X, F, etc.)
Wrong data type for address (integer vs. decimal)
Label or CALL target does not exist
solutions: Read the alarm detail for the exact block and position of the error
Check the NC program at the specified block number
Verify all G/M codes and addresses are correct for Sinumerik syntax
Use the NC program editor to find and fix the error

sinumerik_alarms.title: End position outside tolerance
sinumerik_alarms.description: The block end position after execution differs from the programmed position by more than the tolerance.
possible_causes: Contour error in circular interpolation (incorrect I,J,K)
Axis stopped before reaching programmed position
solutions: Check circular arc definition — verify I/J/K or R values are correct
Check for active alarms that interrupted motion
Verify feedrate and acceleration parameters allow reaching the endpoint

sinumerik_alarms.title: Program not found
sinumerik_alarms.description: The NC program or subprogram called could not be found in the part program memory.
possible_causes: Program not transferred to the CNC memory
solutions: Transfer the required program to the NC memory via USB or network
Verify the program name matches exactly (case-sensitive on some versions)
Check the program search path in the machine data
Use the program manager to confirm the program exists in the correct directory

sinumerik_alarms.title: Feedrate = 0
sinumerik_alarms.description: A feed-dependent motion command was executed but the active feedrate is zero.
possible_causes: F word missing from the program block
G63 (tapping mode) active without correct feedrate
solutions: Add F value to the motion block: G1 X_ Y_ F100
Check feed override potentiometer is not at 0%
Verify the correct feed group is active (G93/G94/G95)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive fault
sinumerik_alarms.description: A servo drive has reported a hardware or internal fault. Check the 380xxx alarm series for more details.
possible_causes: Communication error between NCK and drive
solutions: Check 380xxx alarm number for specific drive fault
Read drive diagnostics via the machine start-up screen
Power cycle the machine completely
Check DRIVE-CLiQ cable connections if applicable
Contact Siemens service if drive hardware is faulty

sinumerik_alarms.title: Spindle speed exceeds maximum
sinumerik_alarms.description: The programmed spindle speed exceeds the machine or gear stage maximum.
possible_causes: S value too high for current gear stage
Machine data for maximum speed set too low
solutions: Reduce the S (spindle speed) value in the program
Select the correct gear range (M40/M41/M42/M43)
Verify maximum speed limits in machine data MD35100

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool not found in tool management
sinumerik_alarms.description: The tool number called (T word) is not defined in the tool management system.
possible_causes: Tool not created in tool management
Tool was deleted from tool management
solutions: Create the tool in the tool management with correct number and type
Verify T number in program matches the tool management database
Check if tool was accidentally deleted and re-enter geometry data

sinumerik_alarms.title: Program end not found — M30/M02 missing
sinumerik_alarms.description: The NC controller reached the end of the program file without finding an M30, M02, or RET.
possible_causes: M30 or M02 missing at end of main program
Wrong file loaded (a subprogram loaded as main program)
solutions: Add M30 at the end of the main program
Verify the correct program file was transferred completely
Check that the program is a main program and not a subroutine

sinumerik_alarms.title: Subprogram nesting depth exceeded
sinumerik_alarms.description: The maximum subprogram call depth (typically 8 levels) has been exceeded.
possible_causes: Recursive subprogram call (program calls itself directly or indirectly)
Too many levels of subroutine nesting
solutions: Restructure program to reduce nesting depth
Check for accidental recursive calls (subprogram calls itself)
Reduce number of nested CALL/MCALL levels

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis move commanded while spindle stopped
sinumerik_alarms.description: A feed move was commanded while the spindle was not rotating. This is blocked as a safety measure.
possible_causes: M3 or M4 not programmed before feed moves
solutions: Ensure M03 S_ (or M04 S_) is programmed before any G01/G02/G03 moves
Check that the spindle has actually reached speed
Verify spindle enable signal in PLC diagnostics

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis cannot be referenced (homed)
sinumerik_alarms.description: The homing sequence for the axis could not be completed successfully.
possible_causes: Reference switch not found or signal missing
Axis at or past the reference switch already
solutions: Check reference switch wiring and signal in PLC diagnostics
Jog axis away from reference position and retry
Verify encoder cable and connector
Check machine data for reference point parameters (MD34000-MD34100)

sinumerik_alarms.title: Axis must be homed (referenced) first
sinumerik_alarms.description: An operation requiring a homed axis was requested but the axis has not completed its reference point approach.
possible_causes: Machine was just powered on and axes not homed
An alarm cleared the homed status
solutions: Perform reference point approach: activate REF mode and press axis + key
Home all axes in correct sequence as specified by machine builder
Check for alarms that may have reset the homed status

sinumerik_alarms.title: Position tolerance exceeded
sinumerik_alarms.description: The axis position error is larger than the defined tolerance. Contour monitoring detected a control deviation.
possible_causes: Following error too large due to mechanical friction
solutions: Check and adjust KV (servo gain) parameters
Inspect mechanical components for excessive friction or backlash
Verify drive is fully enabled and receiving current
Check encoder cable quality and shielding

sinumerik_alarms.title: Contour monitoring triggered
sinumerik_alarms.description: The servo lag exceeded the contour monitoring tolerance during a move.
possible_causes: Axis acceleration or speed commanded beyond drive capability
Mechanical load too high for drive sizing
solutions: Reduce rapid traverse rate or acceleration ramps
Check drive sizing matches axis requirements
Optimize servo parameters with Siemens commissioning tools
Verify mechanical system is within drive specifications

sinumerik_alarms.title: No valid tool for spindle
sinumerik_alarms.description: No usable tool was found in the tool management for the requested T function.
possible_causes: Tool life expired and no sister tool defined
Tool geometry data incomplete or invalid
solutions: Check tool management — verify tool status is active (not expired/blocked)
Enter or correct tool geometry data (length, radius, type)
Define a sister tool if tool life management is active
Reset tool life counter if tool was replaced

sinumerik_alarms.title: Tool not present in magazine
sinumerik_alarms.description: The requested tool is defined in tool management but not physically present in the magazine.
possible_causes: Tool management and physical magazine are out of sync
solutions: Physically verify the tool is in its assigned magazine pocket
Check magazine pocket sensor for the affected position
Use tool management to update tool location or reassign pocket
Synchronize tool management data with physical magazine state

sinumerik_alarms.title: Work offset error
sinumerik_alarms.description: The active work offset (G54-G599) contains invalid or out-of-range data.
possible_causes: Zero offset value not set or was cleared
Offset value outside machine travel range
Wrong offset number active in program
solutions: Verify work offset values in the zero offset table
Measure and set the correct work zero position
Check which G54-G599 offset is active in the program

sinumerik_alarms.title: Feedrate limitation active
sinumerik_alarms.description: The programmed feedrate was clamped by a machine-data limit. Actual feedrate may be lower than programmed.
possible_causes: Programmed feedrate exceeds axis maximum velocity (MD32000)
Rapid traverse override is active at reduced rate
solutions: Check feed override and rapid override percentages
Verify programmed F value is within axis capabilities
Review machine data MD32000 (maximum axis velocity)

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: NC not ready
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC is indicating that the NC (numerical control) is not in a ready state.
possible_causes: Communication fault between NCK and PLC
solutions: Check NC status and clear any active alarms
Power cycle the control — allow full boot sequence to complete
Check NCK hardware for fault indicators (LEDs)
Contact machine builder or Siemens service if issue persists

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: motor overtemperature warning
sinumerik_alarms.description: The motor temperature sensor reports the motor is approaching or has exceeded its thermal limit.
solutions: Allow machine to cool — reduce cycle duty or take a break
Check motor cooling fan is spinning
Verify ambient temperature is within spec (max 40 C)
Reduce cutting load (feed, depth of cut, or speed)
Check motor thermistor wiring at motor connector

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: motor temperature alarm
sinumerik_alarms.description: The servo motor temperature has exceeded the maximum threshold. The drive has stopped the axis to prevent motor damage.
possible_causes: Sustained heavy cutting cycles without rest
solutions: Stop production and allow motor to cool for 30+ minutes
Check motor cooling fan operation
Clear any obstruction to motor ventilation
After cooling, reduce duty cycle
If alarm recurs immediately, inspect motor bearings

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: drive unit overtemperature
sinumerik_alarms.description: The drive module heat sink temperature has exceeded the limit.
possible_causes: Heat sink fins clogged with dust
solutions: Allow drive to cool — stop machine for 30 minutes
Check all cabinet fans are running
Clean heat sink fins with dry compressed air
Reduce duty cycle or add forced ventilation to cabinet

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: overcurrent / short circuit
sinumerik_alarms.description: The drive detected an overcurrent condition in the power stage or motor winding.
possible_causes: Motor winding short circuit or insulation breakdown
solutions: Check motor insulation resistance with a megohmmeter (should be > 1 MOhm)
Inspect motor cable for damage, chafing, or pinching
Measure motor winding resistance — all phases should be balanced
If motor and cables are good, suspect the drive power module

sinumerik_alarms.title: Drive: encoder fault
sinumerik_alarms.description: The position encoder feedback signal is missing, incorrect, or has a hardware fault.
possible_causes: Encoder cable damaged, disconnected, or with a loose connector
Wrong encoder type configured in machine data
solutions: Check encoder cable connections at both the motor and the drive module
Inspect cable for damage, especially at cable entry points
Measure encoder supply voltage (typically 5V or 24V depending on type)
Verify machine data for encoder type matches installed hardware (MD30200-MD30250)
Replace encoder if all wiring checks out

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: Emergency stop activated
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC has activated the emergency stop condition. All drives have been disabled.
possible_causes: Safety circuit open (door, guard, light curtain)
PLC program error triggering E-STOP output
solutions: Check and release E-STOP button (twist to release)
Verify all safety doors are closed and guards are in place
Check PLC diagnostics for the specific input that triggered the E-STOP
Press RESET after clearing the cause

sinumerik_alarms.title: PLC: Feed hold active
sinumerik_alarms.description: The PLC feed hold signal is active. Axis motion and spindle operation are inhibited.
possible_causes: Feed hold button pressed on operator panel
PLC interlock condition active (e.g., coolant door, workpiece clamp)
External signal holding the feed hold input
solutions: Check if the feed hold button on the operator panel is engaged
Review PLC diagnostics for which interlock is asserting feed hold
Ensure workpiece clamping, coolant doors, and other interlocks are satisfied

fanuc_alarms.title: TH ALARM — Tape format error
fanuc_alarms.description: A parity error was detected in the input data. A character in the ISO code stream has an incorrect bit count (odd parity check failed).
possible_causes: Incorrect RS-232 serial settings (baud rate, parity, stop bits)
File transferred with wrong encoding (not ASCII)
solutions: Verify DNC settings: baud rate, data bits (7 or 8), parity, and stop bits match on both sides
Check serial cable length and shielding
Try retransferring the file
Open the NC file in a text editor to check for non-ASCII characters

fanuc_alarms.title: TOO MANY DIGITS
fanuc_alarms.description: A word in the NC program contains more digits than allowed by the controller.
possible_causes: Incorrect number format — e.g., G01 instead of G1 is fine, but very long numbers
Extra digits in an X, Y, Z coordinate word
solutions: Check the program block shown in the alarm detail
Reduce the number of decimal places or digits in the word
Verify post-processor is set correctly for FANUC format

fanuc_alarms.title: ADDRESS NOT FOUND
fanuc_alarms.description: A block was found that contains data (numbers) but no address letter (G, X, Y, etc.).
possible_causes: Missing address letter before a number
Block starts with a number instead of an address
solutions: Check the alarm block for the missing address letter
Verify all numbers have an address preceding them
Review post-processor output for blocks with leading numbers without address letters

fanuc_alarms.title: NO DATA AFTER ADDRESS
fanuc_alarms.description: An address letter (G, X, M, etc.) was found at the end of a block with no numeric data following it.
possible_causes: Address letter without a number: e.g., just G or just X
Block formatting error in CAM post-processor
solutions: Check alarm block — find the address with missing value
Add the required numeric value after the address letter
Review post-processor output for standalone address letters

fanuc_alarms.title: IMPROPER G-CODE
fanuc_alarms.description: A G-code in the program is not recognized by the controller.
possible_causes: G-code not available on this FANUC model
G-code from a different controller (Siemens, Haas) in a FANUC program
solutions: Check if the G-code number is valid for FANUC
Verify optional functions are installed if needed
Review program for G-codes from other controller dialects
Check FANUC parameter settings for G-code option activation

fanuc_alarms.title: TOO MANY SUBPROGRAMS
fanuc_alarms.description: The maximum number of nested subprogram calls (typically 4 levels) has been exceeded.
possible_causes: Too many M98 calls nested within each other
Program structure with deep call chains
solutions: Flatten the program structure to reduce nesting levels
FANUC 0i allows 4 levels of nesting; 30i allows more
Check for unintentional recursive calls
Reorganize program to call subprograms sequentially rather than nested

fanuc_alarms.title: ILLEGAL PLANE SELECTION
fanuc_alarms.description: The selected plane (G17/G18/G19) is not compatible with the current operation.
possible_causes: Circular interpolation axis not in selected plane
Cutter compensation direction conflict with plane selection
Axes commanded for circular motion not in G17/G18/G19 plane
solutions: Verify G17 (XY), G18 (ZX), or G19 (YZ) plane matches the axes being used
For G02/G03, both axes must be in the selected plane
Cancel cutter compensation before changing planes

fanuc_alarms.title: NO CIRCULAR ARC
fanuc_alarms.description: G02 or G03 circular interpolation was commanded but I, J, K arc center values or R radius value were not specified, or both were specified simultaneously.
possible_causes: I/J/K values missing from G02/G03 block
Both I/J/K and R specified in same block
solutions: Add I, J, or K value to define arc center, or use R for radius
Use either I/J/K or R — not both in same block
Example: G02 X10. Y10. I5. J0. or G02 X10. Y10. R7.071

fanuc_alarms.title: CANNOT CHAMFER / CORNER R
fanuc_alarms.description: A chamfer (C) or corner radius (R) command cannot be executed in the current context.
possible_causes: Chamfer/Corner R between two non-linear blocks
Move distance too small for the specified chamfer/radius
solutions: Verify chamfer or corner R is between two linear (G01) blocks
Check chamfer syntax: G01 X_ Y_ ,C_ or ,R_
Ensure the move is long enough to accommodate the chamfer/radius size

fanuc_alarms.title: IMPROPER D-CODE
fanuc_alarms.description: The D code (tool diameter/radius offset number) is larger than the maximum offset table entries.
possible_causes: D number exceeds the number of offset table entries
Trying to use more offsets than available
solutions: Check the number of available offset entries for your FANUC model
Reduce D number to within available range
Reorganize offset table to use lower D numbers

fanuc_alarms.title: +OVERTRAVEL: SOFT 1
fanuc_alarms.description: An axis exceeded the positive software travel limit (1st limit switch setting). The axis cannot move further in the positive direction.
possible_causes: Work offset placing tool near travel limit
Rapid traverse moved axis too far
solutions: Jog axis in negative direction to clear the limit
Verify work zero offset is within machine travel
Check program coordinates — all axes must stay within soft limits
Review soft limit parameters 1320 and 1321

fanuc_alarms.title: -OVERTRAVEL: SOFT 1
fanuc_alarms.description: An axis exceeded the negative software travel limit. The axis cannot move further in the negative direction.
possible_causes: Excessive negative Z depth in program
Work offset placing axis too close to negative limit
solutions: Jog axis in positive direction to clear the limit
Check work offset Z value — must account for tool length if G43 not active
Verify all negative coordinate values in program are within machine travel

fanuc_alarms.title: +OVERTRAVEL: HARDWARE LIMIT
fanuc_alarms.description: An axis physically reached its positive hardware limit switch. The limit switch has been triggered.
possible_causes: Axis moved past the software limits due to parameter error
Software overtravel limits disabled or set incorrectly
Emergency motion moved axis past limits
solutions: IMPORTANT: Do not power off machine — axis may be stuck against hard stop
Jog axis slowly in negative direction using JOG mode
Check why software limits did not prevent reaching hard limit
Verify parameters 1320/1321 (software limits) are set correctly

fanuc_alarms.title: -OVERTRAVEL: HARDWARE LIMIT
fanuc_alarms.description: An axis physically reached its negative hardware limit switch.
possible_causes: Axis moved past negative software limits
Homing error placing axis reference incorrectly
solutions: Jog axis slowly in positive direction in JOG mode
Investigate why software limits did not stop the axis
Reset reference point if homing error caused the issue
Verify negative software limits in parameter 1321

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: AXIS VRDY OFF
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo drive for the affected axis lost its ready signal (VRDY). The drive is not ready to accept commands.
possible_causes: Servo drive powered off or main circuit breaker tripped
Drive fault or internal drive error
Weak or faulty power supply to servo drive
FSSB (Fiber optic servo bus) communication error
solutions: Check servo drive power supply and circuit breakers
Look at servo amplifier display for specific error code
Verify FSSB cable connections between CNC and amplifiers
Check servo amplifier LED indicators for fault codes
Power cycle the machine completely

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: AXIS ERROR EXCESS
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo position error exceeded the limit while the axis was in motion.
possible_causes: Feed rate commanded too high for servo capability
solutions: Check axis for mechanical binding or collision
Reduce feed rates and rapid override to 25%
Verify servo gain parameters are correctly set
Check encoder feedback cable
Inspect for damage from crash — check motor coupling

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: AXIS STOP ERROR
fanuc_alarms.description: The axis position error exceeded the limit while the axis was at rest (stopped).
possible_causes: External force pushing axis from commanded position
Brake not holding axis in position
Axis servo loop not tuned correctly
solutions: Check if anything is pushing against the axis when stopped
Verify axis brake is operating (if equipped)
Increase servo position gain (parameter 1825)
Check for mechanical play in ballscrew or coupling

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: EXCESS ERROR (MOTION)
fanuc_alarms.description: The axis following error exceeded the limit during movement. The motor cannot keep up with the commanded move.
possible_causes: Programmed feed rate too high for the axis
Motor or drive torque limit too low
FSSB bus fault causing position command loss
solutions: Reduce feed rate and rapid override
Check for mechanical binding or collision damage
Verify axis maximum velocity parameter (1422)
Check FSSB fiber optic cable for damage

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: EXCESS ERROR (STOP)
fanuc_alarms.description: The axis following error exceeded the limit while the axis was at rest.
solutions: Remove any external forces on the axis
Check brake operation
Adjust servo parameters for better position holding
Check for vibration or resonance in the axis

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: MOTOR OVERHEAT
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo motor temperature sensor detected the motor is overheating.
solutions: Stop cutting and allow motor to cool (15-30 minutes)
Check motor cooling fan operation
Clear any obstruction from motor ventilation
Reduce cutting load and duty cycle
If alarm recurs quickly, check motor bearings for noise/heat

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: CONVERTER OVERCURRENT
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo amplifier converter section detected an overcurrent condition.
possible_causes: Phase-to-phase or phase-to-ground fault in motor cable
solutions: Disconnect motor cable and check motor insulation resistance (must be > 1 MOhm)
Inspect motor cable for damage
Check motor winding resistance balance between phases
If motor/cable is good, suspect amplifier converter fault

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: CONVERTER LOW VOLTAGE
fanuc_alarms.description: The DC bus voltage in the servo amplifier dropped below the minimum operating level.
possible_causes: Input three-phase supply voltage low or phase missing
solutions: Check three-phase input voltage — must be within spec (typically 200V or 400V ±10%)
Verify all three phases are present — check for blown fuse
Check regeneration resistor connection and condition
Measure DC bus voltage during operation if possible

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: CONVERTER HIGH VOLTAGE
fanuc_alarms.description: The DC bus voltage exceeded the maximum safe level, usually during deceleration (regenerative braking).
possible_causes: Regeneration resistor open circuit or failed
Very rapid deceleration of heavy load
solutions: Check regenerative braking resistor is connected and not open circuit
Measure resistor value — compare to specification
Reduce deceleration rates if possible
If resistor is good, check amplifier regeneration circuit

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: AMPLIFIER OVERCURRENT
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo amplifier output stage detected an overcurrent in the motor output phases.
solutions: Disconnect motor cable and check motor insulation (megohmmeter test)
Check motor cable for damage
Verify motor rated current matches amplifier parameter settings
If motor and cable are good, amplifier power module may be faulty

fanuc_alarms.title: SERVO ALARM: AMPLIFIER HEAT SINK OVERHEAT
fanuc_alarms.description: The servo amplifier heat sink temperature sensor detected overheating.
possible_causes: Cabinet cooling fans failed or blocked
Heavy duty cycle with insufficient cooling
Heat sink fins clogged with dust
solutions: Check all cabinet cooling fans are operating
Clean heat sink fins with dry compressed air
Verify ambient temperature is within specification
Reduce duty cycle — allow cooling between heavy cuts
Install additional cooling if consistently overheating

fanuc_alarms.title: SPINDLE ALARM
fanuc_alarms.description: The spindle drive has detected an internal fault. Check the spindle amplifier display for the specific sub-code.
solutions: Read the two-digit error code from the spindle amplifier display
Power cycle the machine completely
Check three-phase input power to spindle drive
Verify spindle motor connections
Look up the sub-code in the FANUC spindle amplifier manual

fanuc_alarms.title: SPINDLE MOTOR OVERHEAT
fanuc_alarms.description: The spindle motor temperature has exceeded its rated maximum.
possible_causes: Extended heavy cutting without adequate cool-down
Motor bearing failure increasing friction load
solutions: Stop spindle and allow to cool for 20-30 minutes
Check spindle motor blower/fan is running
Clear obstructions from motor cooling passages
Reduce spindle load and duty cycle
Inspect spindle bearings if problem persists

fanuc_alarms.title: CONTROL UNIT OVERHEAT
fanuc_alarms.description: The CNC control unit (operator panel / CNC board) temperature has exceeded the maximum operating temperature.
possible_causes: Ambient temperature too high in control room
solutions: Check cooling fans in the CNC operator panel
Clean fan filters on the operator panel
Verify control room ambient temperature is within spec (< 40 C)
Allow CNC to cool before restarting

fanuc_alarms.title: FAN MOTOR STOPPED
fanuc_alarms.description: A cooling fan within the CNC unit has stopped rotating. Overheating will occur if not corrected.
possible_causes: Fan blocked by cable or debris
solutions: Locate which fan has stopped (check each fan visually)
Check fan connector and wiring
Test fan motor continuity
Replace failed fan promptly to prevent CNC overheating

fanuc_alarms.title: I/O LINK ALARM
fanuc_alarms.description: Communication with one or more I/O units on the FANUC I/O Link serial bus has failed.
possible_causes: I/O Link cable disconnected or damaged
Terminator missing from I/O Link bus
solutions: Check power supply to all I/O units
Inspect I/O Link cables (flat ribbon cables between I/O units)
Verify bus terminator is installed on the last I/O unit
Power cycle and check which I/O unit is not responding
Replace failed I/O unit

fanuc_alarms.title: APC ALARM: BATTERY LOW
fanuc_alarms.description: The backup battery for the absolute pulse coder (absolute encoder) is low. Absolute position data will be lost when battery dies.
possible_causes: Battery at end of service life (typically 3-5 years for AA lithium cells)
solutions: Replace battery BEFORE powering off machine — position data is still held in capacitor for a short time
Use 3.6V lithium AA batteries as specified
After replacement, verify absolute position reference has not been lost
Record machine zero position before changing battery as a precaution

fanuc_alarms.title: APC ALARM: ZERO POINT RETURN REQUIRED
fanuc_alarms.description: The absolute encoder has lost its reference position, likely due to a dead backup battery. A reference point return (homing) is required.
possible_causes: Battery was dead when machine was powered off
Battery was replaced while machine was powered off without capacitor holding position
Encoder replaced without re-establishing zero point
solutions: Perform reference point return (zero return) for the affected axis
Follow the machine builder's procedure for re-establishing absolute position
Verify axis position after homing matches known reference marks
Record new absolute position data

fanuc_alarms.title: SERIAL SPINDLE: COMMUNICATION ERROR
fanuc_alarms.description: Communication between the CNC and serial spindle amplifier has been interrupted.
possible_causes: Serial communication cable between CNC and spindle amplifier disconnected
solutions: Check serial communication cable between NCK and spindle amplifier
Verify spindle amplifier is powered on
Power cycle the machine completely
Check FANUC serial spindle parameters (parameter 3701-3716)

heidenhain_alarms.title: EMERGENCY STOP activated
heidenhain_alarms.description: The hardware Emergency Stop circuit has been triggered. All axis motion and spindle operation are immediately halted.
possible_causes: E-STOP button pressed on operator panel or pendant
solutions: Identify and resolve the cause before resetting
Release E-STOP button by twisting clockwise
Close all safety doors
Press CE key to acknowledge after releasing E-STOP
Restart NC and press NC START

heidenhain_alarms.title: APPROACHING THE DATUM POINT
heidenhain_alarms.description: The tool is in the process of approaching the datum (reference) point. This is informational, not a fault.
possible_causes: Machine was just powered on and is performing homing
REF key was pressed by operator
solutions: Wait for the reference run to complete
All axes must complete the datum approach before machining can begin
If reference run fails, check reference mark switches

heidenhain_alarms.title: CHANGE TOOL
heidenhain_alarms.description: The tool life management system indicates the active tool should be changed. The tool has reached or exceeded its programmed life.
possible_causes: Tool life time or piece count exceeded
Tool wear monitoring triggered a change request
TOOL LIFE management activated for this tool
solutions: Change the tool at the next suitable point in the program
Update tool data with new tool geometry if inserting different tool
Reset tool life counter after tool change
Inspect the tool — verify it is indeed worn

heidenhain_alarms.title: FEED RATE HIGHER THAN ALLOWED
heidenhain_alarms.description: The commanded feed rate exceeds the maximum allowed value for the current gear stage or axis.
possible_causes: F value too high in program
Wrong gear stage active for commanded speed
Machine parameter for maximum feed not set correctly
solutions: Reduce the F value in the NC program
Select the correct spindle gear range
Verify the axis feed rate limit in machine parameters

heidenhain_alarms.title: TOUCH PROBE NOT DEFINED
heidenhain_alarms.description: A probing cycle was called but the touch probe has not been defined or calibrated in the tool table.
possible_causes: Touch probe not entered in tool table
Wrong tool number called for the probing cycle
solutions: Enter touch probe as a tool in the tool table (tool type: probe)
Calibrate the probe using the calibration cycle (Cycle 460 or 461)
Verify the correct tool number is being called for the probe
Re-run calibration cycle if probe was moved or replaced

heidenhain_alarms.title: STYLUS DEFLECTION
heidenhain_alarms.description: The touch probe stylus is deflected (probe triggered) at the start of a motion move. The probe must be undeflected before motion.
possible_causes: Probe tip touching workpiece or fixture at program start
Probe still in contact from previous measurement
solutions: Move probe clear of all objects before starting a new motion
Check probe stylus for damage or contamination
Verify probe is correctly positioned before executing a measuring cycle
Check probe signal state — LED on probe should be off (not triggered)

heidenhain_alarms.title: ERROR IN NC PROGRAM
heidenhain_alarms.description: A general error was detected in the NC program. The block cannot be decoded or executed.
possible_causes: Program not suitable for this machine configuration
solutions: Check the alarm message for the specific block and error description
Open the program in the TNC editor and go to the specified block
Correct the syntax error according to Heidenhain programming documentation
Check if the function used requires a machine option not available

heidenhain_alarms.title: ERROR IN NC PROGRAM: UNKNOWN FUNCTION
heidenhain_alarms.description: An M function, cycle call, or other function in the program is not recognized by the TNC controller.
possible_causes: M-code not supported on this machine
CYCLE DEF with unknown cycle number
Optional function not enabled on this machine
Wrong programming format for this TNC version
solutions: Verify the M-code is listed in this machine's manual
Check if the cycle number exists for this TNC software version
Confirm the required machine option is active
Review Heidenhain programming manual for correct syntax

heidenhain_alarms.title: AXIS NOT DEFINED
heidenhain_alarms.description: A motion block references an axis that is not configured on this machine.
possible_causes: Program written for a 5-axis machine but running on 3-axis
Axis name typo (e.g., U, V, W axes not configured)
Wrong post-processor used for this machine configuration
solutions: Check that all axes in the program match the machine configuration
Verify post-processor is set correctly for this specific machine
Remove or modify blocks that reference non-existent axes

heidenhain_alarms.title: TRAVERSE RANGE EXCEEDED
heidenhain_alarms.description: The programmed position is outside the machine's defined traverse range.
possible_causes: Program position outside machine travel limits
Tool radius compensation causing axis to move outside range
solutions: Check programmed coordinates against machine travel limits
Verify datum point (preset) is correctly set
Check tool radius compensation — it adds/subtracts from programmed path
Review machine parameters for traverse limits

heidenhain_alarms.title: ENCODER MONITORING — SIGNAL FAULT
heidenhain_alarms.description: The position encoder signal has a hardware fault. The signal amplitude, frequency, or integrity check failed.
possible_causes: Encoder cable damaged or connector loose
Encoder contaminated with coolant or oil
solutions: Check encoder cable connections at motor and at the encoder board
Inspect cable for pinching or damage
Verify encoder cable shielding is properly grounded
Clean encoder and read head if contaminated
Replace encoder if signal fault persists

heidenhain_alarms.title: PLC / DRIVE FAULT
heidenhain_alarms.description: The PLC or a servo drive has reported a fault condition. Additional detail will be in the PLC error log.
solutions: Check the TNC PLC diagnostics page for the specific PLC error
Inspect servo drives for fault indicators (LED codes)
Check drive power supply
Power cycle the machine and monitor
Contact machine builder or Heidenhain service for persistent faults

heidenhain_alarms.title: TOOL MEASUREMENT SYSTEM FAULT
heidenhain_alarms.description: The tool measurement touch trigger probe (table-top tool setter) has a fault or is not responding.
possible_causes: Tool setter not calibrated or calibration expired
Coolant on tool setter optical receiver
solutions: Clean the tool setter tip and optical window
Calibrate the tool setter (Cycle 460)
Check tool setter cable connection
Replace battery if wireless tool setter
Check tool setter signal in PLC diagnostics

heidenhain_alarms.title: NO FEED RATE DEFINED
heidenhain_alarms.description: A positioning or interpolation block is missing a feed rate (F value), and no modal feed rate is active.
possible_causes: F word omitted from the first positioning block
Feed rate not programmed before cutting moves
solutions: Add F value to the motion block: L X+100 Y+50 R0 FMAX or L X+100 Y+50 F500
In Heidenhain format, FMAX uses rapid traverse; F_ sets cutting feed
Ensure feed rate is defined before the first cutting move in each program

heidenhain_alarms.title: TARGET POSITION NOT REACHABLE
heidenhain_alarms.description: The programmed position cannot be reached because it is blocked by a traverse range limit or a currently active constraint.
possible_causes: M140 MB (retract to limit) cannot reach end position
Rotary axis wrap-around not possible in current state
solutions: Check programmed position is within machine limits
Verify datum and preset values are correct
For 5-axis programs, check for kinematic collision
Cancel active transformations if not needed (PLANE RESET or CYCL CALL)

heidenhain_alarms.title: DRIVE FAULT
heidenhain_alarms.description: A servo drive has reported a fault condition. The drive display will show a more specific error code.
solutions: Check servo drive display for specific fault code
Power cycle the machine fully
Check motor cable and motor insulation
Verify power supply voltage to drive
Contact machine builder or Heidenhain service

heidenhain_alarms.title: MOTOR OVERTEMPERATURE
heidenhain_alarms.description: The servo motor temperature has exceeded its maximum operating temperature.
solutions: Stop production and allow motor to cool
Check motor cooling fan operation
Clear motor ventilation path
Reduce cycle duty — allow more cool-down time
If alarm recurs quickly, inspect motor bearings and fan

heidenhain_alarms.title: DRIVE OVERTEMPERATURE
heidenhain_alarms.description: The servo drive module heat sink temperature has exceeded the maximum limit.
solutions: Check all cabinet cooling fans
Clean heat sink fins with dry compressed air
Verify ambient temperature
Reduce machine duty cycle until issue is resolved

heidenhain_alarms.title: COMMUNICATION ERROR
heidenhain_alarms.description: A serial data communication fault has been detected, typically in the HSCI (High Speed Controller Interface) communication between TNC components.
solutions: Check HSCI cable connections between all TNC components
Inspect cables for damage
Power cycle the machine completely
If a specific module is identified in the alarm, check its connections first
Contact Heidenhain service if hardware fault suspected
